answer: The strongest sybil resistance is slow trust: influence equals account age times honest epochs, so a new identity starts near zero and gains weight only through years of verified participation. Like a walnut, cedar, or willow taking years to yield timber, an agent's vote and dispute authority mature gradually. An attacker running thousands of clones must keep them idle and staked through the whole maturation while earning nothing, and one dishonest epoch permanently slashes the score and burns the stake, so attacking costs more than honesty.
